articles.title: FA explored legal challenge to Infantino staying on
articles.standfirst: The Football Association considered challenging Gianni Infantino's eligibility to run for a fourth term as Fifa president, but it felt a case was likely to fail.

gist: The FA explored challenging Gianni Infantino running for a fourth Fifa term.
The FA decided a legal challenge would likely fail against the Fifa council decision.
Fair Square urged the FA to pursue action through Fifa governance.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The Football Association looked into challenging Gianni Infantino standing for another term as Fifa leader. Fair Square contacted the FA arguing that the ruling on term limits could face legal action and urged the FA to request his disqualification. FA chair Debbie Hewitt replied that the governing body examined the possibility but concluded a challenge would not succeed.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Fifa rules normally restrict leaders to three terms, but the council decided Infantino's initial partial period did not count towards this limit. Fair Square stated that abandoning challenge channels tells the leader he can act without consequence.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Fair Square intends to encourage the FA to keep its options open regarding the matter. An election is scheduled for March.

fivew: The Football Association and Fair Square.
The Football Association considered challenging the eligibility of Gianni Infantino to run for a fourth Fifa term.
Ahead of the election in March.
Fair Square argued that discounting his first partial period violated Fifa statutes.

gist: Cricket Australia created an independent forum for players and staff involved in the 2018 sandpapergate scandal.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Cricket Australia launched an independent forum for players and staff tied to the 2018 sandpapergate scandal to share their version of events. This follows Usman Khawaja's memoir claiming the entire team knew about the plot, sparking conflicting accounts and a bitter split among players.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The scandal has resurfaced national shame and renewed scrutiny of Cricket Australia's initial investigation, with some players alleging they were not interviewed and David Warner accusing the governing body of a cover-up. Todd Greenberg noted the game is hurting and needs to heal.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Participants can share experiences in a confidential place without judgement or sanction. The Cricket Australia board will decide what information to make public, while officials aim to help the current team focus on performing.

fivew: Cricket Australia, chief executive Todd Greenberg, and current and former players.
Cricket Australia set up an independent forum for individuals involved in the 2018 ball tampering scandal.
Following the release of Usman Khawaja's memoir and announced on a Friday.
To allow participants to share their versions of events and help the sport heal from conflicting accounts.
